newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end 1.95 pct down on economic jitters.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end 1.95 pct down on economic jitters.

text.p: Thai stocks finished sharply lower for the third straight session on Friday as investors continued showing jitters about weak economic indicators and talks on loan defaults faced by financial institutions, brokers said.

The SET index ended 15.66 points, or 1.95 percent, lower at a near 52-month low of 787.47 on thin 3.06 billion baht turnover. The index last closed lower on September 9, 1992, at 782.85. The SET-50 index ended 1.36 points down at 57.73.
"Rumours on some financial institutions facing loan default problems hit the market today," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance and Securities.
Brokers said the rumours since last week prompted investors to unload bank and finance shares on Friday.
Investors have been disappointed by sluggish exports and high Thai current account deficit of 8.2 percent of gross domestic product in 1996.

All large capitalised banks and finance firms suffered losses. Bangkok Bank topped the active list, ending unchanged at 186 baht, Thai Farmers Bank fell two to 121, and Finance One slipped 3.50 to 41.25.
